q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a padlock?
title: Padlock carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the metals in each lock, such as brass, zinc alloy and steel, and multiply each by its supplier's per-kg figure. Add casting, machining, plating, assembly and packing energy, then divide the plant's energy by locks passed.

ul: Body: brass, zinc die cast, iron or steel by weight.
Shackle, springs and levers in steel.
Keys in brass or nickel silver.
Casting or forging the body, with furnace fuel.
Machining, polishing and nickel or chrome plating.
Assembly, testing and blister or box packing.

p: Report per lock by model and size. Metal is usually the largest share, so record weights from the bill of materials.

example.title: Worked example: lock unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 17,180 / 50,000 = 0.344 kg CO2 per lock
Add brass, zinc and steel for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
